pageCache.pageTitle: Leonard Stanley C. of E. (Aided) Primary School - Home Page
pageCache.text:
Welcome to an exciting adventure
We are a Church of England primary school located near Stroud in Gloucestershire. We have a very experienced and talented staff who provide a fantastic all-round education for just over 225 children, from 3-11 years old, in accordance with our Christian vision, "Loving and Learning together for Life, as Jesus taught us." Our core values are Respect, Resilience and Kindness which permeates through our daily life.
At Leonard Stanley School we offer a broad and balanced curriculum and encourage every child to achieve their very best. Our children are our fantastic ambassadors to our school and we take pride in their achievements. Our curriculum is planned using a focus on reading and experiences to engage children's interest.
We thrive on using our whole school. Our PE curriculum has a focus on cycling, from balance bikes to mountain bikes, Judo, which is taught from Y1 to Y4, and swimming in which every class has 3 sessions a week in the summer term in our school pool. We also utilise our two outdoor classrooms and cooking provision to ensure our curriculum is practical, fun and useful.
We place high value on providing an education that gives the children a wide range of experiences in a safe and friendly environment to enable them to become confident individuals, risk takers and kind human beings. We have regular arts, music and drama events and our children also take part in a wide range of sporting activities.
We hope that our website gives you a picture of life at our school but we welcome visitors, so if you would like to come and see for yourself, please contact the school office.
Leonard Stanley is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment.
Mr Andrew Milner, Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Leonard Stanley C. of E. (Aided) Primary School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum
We consider it important to embrace all the experiences of children in school when planning the curriculum
At Leonard Stanley C of E Primary School, we want our children to develop a love for reading. This is our golden thread that passes throughout our school, from the beginning of early phonics in LSEY (using Twinkl phonics) to a whole-class guided reading approach exploring a range of texts and interests on a regular basis. Our children read every day.
We want all children to be able to access our full curriculum with adaptations implemented, if required. We want to share our exciting curriculum offer and allow all children to reach their potential.
We teach a carefully sequenced, knowledge-rich curriculum that aims to inspire pupils and promote excellent outcomes for all. The curriculum content has been carefully chosen by our own subject experts and is organised in a coherent way, ensuring children can build on their knowledge from year to year. In this way, the knowledge in the curriculum is cumulative, constructing firm foundations and schema from which children can progress and develop deeper conceptual understanding and subject-specific knowledge and skills over time.
Our curriculum also values talk, discussion, and reflection. Children have time to think deeply and learn how to discuss their ideas and opinions, as well as taking time to listen to and understand the ideas of others.
Please look at our curriculum pages to see how each subject is taught throughout their time at Leonard Stanley, and to find out what each class is being taught this year, please look at the class pages.
Please ask your class teacher or any of the school's SLT if you have any questions about our curriculum.

pageCache.pageTitle: Leonard Stanley C. of E. (Aided) Primary School - Our Performance
pageCache.text:
Ofsted & SIAMS reports
Ofsted 2024
Belonging is at the heart of this welcoming and inclusive school. As a result, pupils are excited to come to school. They are invested in the school's values, particularly in being kind . Pupils behave well. They play in harmony across year groups. Pupils show genuine care for others. They have warm relationships with adults. This helps them feel safe.
Pupils contribute to the life of the school in many ways. For example, they get to be eco councillors and take pride in keeping the school environment tidy. Pupils enjoy attending the variety of clubs that have been selected based on their interests. Mountain biking, Bollywood and football clubs are firm favourites.
Ofsted Report Nov2024 (1)
SIAMS Report 2026
The Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools (SIAMS) is the Church of England and Methodist Church’s outworking of the requirements of section 48 of the Education Act 2005. It is a key element of the life of all Church of England and Methodist schools in England.
SIAMS explores ways in which each school’s theologically rooted Christian vision drives its work and enables the school to live up to its foundation as a Church school. It does so by seeking to answer six or (in the case of Voluntary Aided schools) seven Inspection Questions (IQs).
"Leonard Stanley Church of England (Aided) Primary School is living up to its foundation as a Church school and is enabling pupils and adults to flourish."
"The Christian vision, together with its supporting values, is clearly articulated, well understood and lived out in daily practice."
"The well-embedded Christian vision creates a deep sense of love and community."
"Behaviour is exemplary and pupils are proud of their purposeful and happy school."
"This allows them to develop confidence and nurtures their love of learning."
